source.title_on_document: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning

paper_design_summary: Adults recruited online were individually randomized to write an argumentative essay under a self-generation-first Qwen3.5 workflow, a direct-adoption Qwen3.5 workflow, or no AI. All arms were then assigned a parallel essay without AI 15-20 minutes later in the same session; 659 of 900 randomized people were analyzed after exclusions. At least two raters blind to condition and phase scored the essays for reasoning quality, within-essay breadth of perspectives, and originality (pp. 3-7, Sections 2.1-2.8 and Table 2).

studies.label: Three-arm workflow experiment (argumentative essay with or without AI, then unaided parallel essay)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individual assignment to one Phase-1 workflow: Autonomous (self-generation-first AI), Dependent (direct-adoption AI), or No-AI. The same people completed Phase 2 without AI; phase order was fixed. Topic A versus Topic B placement across phases was counterbalanced, crossed with condition (p. 5, Section 2.3). This is between-person assignment with repeated observations, not randomized within-person ordering of AI conditions.
assignment.quote: Participants were assigned by stratified block randomization (strata: baseline-ability tertile crossed with student or worker status; block size six; equal allocation), with the assignment sequence generated and recorded by the online system.
assignment.locator: p. 6, Section 2.8; p. 3, Section 2.1; p. 4, Table 2
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 3, Section 2.1.1: 'The study was not formally preregistered'; primary endpoint, covariates, exclusion criteria, and BH family were fixed in a dated internal analysis plan written before the data were analyzed

arms.name: Autonomous
arms.description: Self-generation-first workflow: interface step-lock required a written position and a 3-5 point outline (at least 80 characters) before the AI panel opened; then a comparison box required recording at least one disagreement with the AI's points and judging which side was better founded; final text had to be rewritten in the participant's own words. (p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5; counts p. 4, Table 2.)

arms.name: Dependent
arms.description: Direct-adoption workflow: no outline step; instructed to have AI generate the arguments and paragraphs and to adopt its output as it stands, with minimal changes (p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5; counts p. 4, Table 2).

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Wrote the Phase-1 essay independently; prohibited from using any AI tool, search engine, or external material. (p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5; counts p. 4, Table 2.)

participants.exclusions: Of 900 randomized people, 659 were analyzed after exclusions. In Autonomous/Dependent/No-AI order, excluded for any reason: 56/69/116; rates 20.1%/23.5%/35.4% (chi2(2) = 20.22, p < 0.0001). Failed attention check: 29/31/29 (89 total); missing Phase 2: 26/39/30 (95 total); long-string responding: 4/2/4 (10 total); AI-authorship screen: 69 in No-AI only. Categories overlap. The AI screen was a single team consensus decision without an independent reliability estimate. The paper labels the primary analysis modified intention-to-treat; it excludes people after assignment and is not a full intention-to-treat analysis. Per-protocol sensitivity analysis: 585 analyzed (172/201/212); available-case sensitivity analysis: 805 analyzed; multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis: all 900 randomized people analyzed (pp. 3-4, Section 2.2 and Table 2; pp. 6-7, Sections 2.6 and 2.8; p. 10, Table 4).
participants.who: Adults who reported using generative AI for cognitive tasks, recruited through an online research participant platform with quotas across student and early-career-worker status; mean age 24.6 years, 54% women (p. 3, Section 2.2). Described as Chinese-speaking students and early-career workers (p. 13, Section 4.5); residence country is not stated.
participants.quote: leaving a primary analysis sample of N = 659 (autonomous = 222, dependent = 225, no-AI = 212; mean age 24.6 years, 54% women).
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 2.2; p. 4, Tables 1-2; p. 13, Section 4.5

ai_tool.name_model: Qwen3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen; Alibaba Cloud), called through the official API with one pinned version and fixed sampling parameters; identical system prompt in both AI arms casting it as a general-purpose Chinese-language writing assistant (p. 5, Section 2.5; the exact pinned identifier and parameter values are offered on request, not printed.)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants interacted with a Qwen3.5 panel embedded in the study platform, using the same model, system prompt, and prompt-template pool in both AI arms. Calls were uncapped (observed range 1-8, median 3). Autonomous participants first submitted a position and outline, then compared, criticized, and rewrote AI content; Dependent participants generated and directly adopted it. Open-chat coding denotes interactive model use, constrained by these assigned workflows. AI was available only in Phase 1; Phase 2 prohibited AI and external tools for everyone (p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5). Mean unrevised adoption of AI content was 32% in Autonomous versus 73% in Dependent (p. 7, Section 3.1).

task.description: Argumentative essays on public-policy questions: Topic A (ban private cars from city centers) and Topic B (move from a 5-day to a 4-day work week), counterbalanced across phases. Phase 1: AI-assisted (or unaided in no-AI arm) essay of 300-500 words. Phase 2: structurally parallel essay of 300-500 words with no AI for any arm. A short unaided baseline essay (homework policy, 120-200 words, 5-7 min) before randomization served as a covariate. (p. 5, Sections 2.3 and 2.5.)
task.duration: Phase 1: 12-15 min limit; Phase 2: 10-12 min limit, 15-20 min after Phase 1 in the same session; baseline essay 5-7 min (p. 5, Sections 2.3 and 2.5). Observed mean Phase-1 time 14.2/13.1/13.3 min and Phase-2 time 11.3/11.8/11.5 min (p. 4, Table 1; Autonomous/Dependent/No-AI order).

outcomes.name: Phase-2 (unaided) reasoning quality
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric for clarity of thesis, relevance and sufficiency of evidence, coherence of reasoning, and handling of counterarguments. Each essay was scored by at least two raters blind to condition and phase; two-or-more-point disagreements went to a third rater; rater means were analyzed. Raters were trained on shared exemplars and calibrated to ICC(2,k) >= 0.75; professional credentials are not stated (p. 6, Section 2.6). Phase-2 ICC(2,k) = 0.86 (p. 7, Section 3.3). Coded usefulness because codebook Section 6 includes quality of a single output; this is argument quality, not an overall-creativity rating. Participant-level ANCOVA adjusts baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time, with No-AI as reference (p. 6, Section 2.8). Reasoning quality is the primary outcome within each task; Dependent versus No-AI in Phase 2 is the single overall primary endpoint (pp. 3 and 6). Robustness variants include per-protocol, HC3, single raters, Phase-1 time/effort/performance adjustments, relaxed exclusions, multiple imputation, and completion-time floors (pp. 9-10, Sections 3.5-3.7 and Table 4). The baseline-to-Phase-2 change-score comparison is a robustness analysis of this outcome: No-AI -0.02, Autonomous +0.17, Dependent -0.49; F(2, 656) = 15.66, p < 0.0001 (p. 12, Section 4.5).
outcomes.delay: 15-20 minutes after Phase 1 in the same session (p. 3, Section 2.1); Phase 2 was unaided in every arm.

outcomes.measure_detail: Same 1-7 reasoning-quality rubric as S1-O1, scored by blind raters and averaged (p. 6, Section 2.6). Phase-1 ICC(2,k) = 0.85 (p. 7, Section 3.3). eligibility.reason: All three criteria are met in S1. The online system individually assigned people by stratified block randomization to two Qwen3.5 generative-AI workflows or No-AI for argumentative essays (p. 5, Sections 2.3-2.5; p. 6, Section 2.8). Of 900 randomized people, 659 were analyzed: Autonomous 222, Dependent 225, No-AI 212 (p. 3, Section 2.2; p. 4, Table 2), exceeding 50 without counting repeated essays or ratings as additional people. Blind raters scored originality and within-essay breadth of perspectives on the submitted essays using 1-7 rubrics; the policy essays admit multiple arguments and meet the creative-task definition despite reasoning quality being the overall primary endpoint (p. 5, Section 2.3; p. 6, Section 2.6). Phase-1 outcomes answer with_ai for the AI-workflow comparison; Phase-2 outcomes answer after_ai because AI was removed for all arms (p. 5, Sections 2.3-2.5). No across_people outcome is reported. Post-randomization exclusions mean the primary analysis is not full intention-to-treat (p. 7, Section 2.8). The remaining documentation questions do not affect any eligibility criterion.

one_line_finding: On the unaided essay 15-20 minutes later, direct-adoption AI reduced reasoning quality (-0.38, d = -0.28) and within-essay flexibility (-0.30, d = -0.23) versus No-AI, but not originality (q = 0.28); self-generation-first did not fall below No-AI (pp. 7-8, Section 3.4).

notes: The full markdown conversion was read, including the references through p. 15; the saved PDF contains no appendix. PDF and printed page numbers agree. Both raw forms parsed. All six distinct phase-by-rubric outcomes are retained; wording differences and information merely repeated in another form field are not counted as substantive differences. Reasoning quality is coded usefulness under the codebook definition of quality of a single output; it is not an overall-creativity rating. The paper identifies reasoning quality as primary within each task (p. 6, Section 2.6), so the shared secondary code for S1-O4 was corrected to paper_primary; only S1-O1 has the single overall primary endpoint (p. 3). The shared treatment_higher code for Autonomous versus No-AI reasoning in Phase 2 was corrected to no_clear_difference under the reported FDR procedure (p. 8). Complete outcome means and SDs by arm are not tabulated; Figure 2A shows adjusted means with +/-1 SE, and Figure 2B shows 95% intervals. In statistics_available, figure_only flags graph-only components such as adjusted arm means or confidence limits, not an absence of all numeric reporting; p_value_only identifies contrasts whose only printed numeric uncertainty is a p value even when the raw difference is also given. A printed difference without an SE is not coded mean_difference_se. No effects, SEs, graph coordinates, or combined Phase-1 sample sizes were computed. Section 2.8 gives an achieved-cell range of 209-225 (p. 6), while the participant section and Table 2 explicitly give 222/225/212; the latter counts are recorded as analyzed. The analyzed Phase-1 AI-arm counts are 222 and 225; a combined total is not separately printed. The Phase-2 originality values -0.07 and d = -0.02 are preserved as printed (p. 8), without recalculation. No Phase-1 AI-versus-No-AI outcome contrast is reported. Trait, mediation, and process-log analyses use some of the same output scores but are not additional distinct creativity outcomes or additional randomized workflow contrasts (pp. 9-11, Sections 3.8-3.10). Both AI workflows are instructed extremes (p. 12, Section 4.4); the paper-designated primary endpoint takes precedence over guessing which arm resembles ordinary chatbot use. Data are not public; de-identified data and analysis materials are available on reasonable request, subject to institutional ethics requirements (p. 13, Data availability statement); no data or code URL is printed. Unresolved reconciliation status refers to source silence about a separate supplement, not to uncertainty over core eligibility. Final review read the complete markdown through the final references and checked the relevant PDF passages, including direct extraction of Tables 1, 2, and 4. The assignment, people, and outcome challenge files each contain an empty problems array, so challenge_resolution is empty and all three challenge-action counts are zero. Finalization makes analyzed-count wording explicit, adds the page locator for observed task durations, and classifies the remaining open documentation items; no recorded numerical result was changed. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged.
